name: pint16f
finding: REVIEW_Aug4 A4-H03 (16-bit protected-mode interrupt/trap gate frames: word frames everywhere -- 6/8-byte same-priv, 10/12-byte cross-priv, SP wraps in the low 16 on a B=0 stack with ESP[31:16] preserved)
transitions: real->protected (CR0.PE 0->1, CS far-jump to code32 0x08 -- ALL code segments are BASED at 0xF0000 so every offset is 16-bit clean and the 16-bit frames' WORD IP slots are exact)

GDT (11 entries): code32 0x08 DPL0 base 0xF0000, data32 0x10 flat, code16 0x18 DPL0 base 0xF0000 (D=0, the 16-bit-gate handler segment), code32 0x20 DPL3 base 0xF0000, data32 0x28 DPL3 flat, data16 0x30 (B=0, the case-5 wrap stack), TSS 0x38 (base 0x4000), code32 0x48 DPL3 NOT-PRESENT (case 4's #NP target), code32 0x50 DPL0 limit 0x100 (case 2's offset-past-limit #GP(0) target); LTR 0x38

IDT: 0x40 16-bit INT gate -> h16_c1; VECTOR 13 (#GP) 16-bit TRAP gate -> h16_c2; 0x42 16-bit INT gate DPL3 -> h16_c3; VECTOR 11 (#NP) 16-bit TRAP gate -> h16_c4; 0x44 16-bit INT gate DPL3 -> h16_c5; 0x45 32-bit INT gate -> h_c7; 0x46 32-bit INT gate DPL3 -> h_c7x

case (1): CPL0 software INT $0x40 through the 16-bit INTERRUPT gate: SP 0x7000 -> 0x6FFA (exactly 6); the handler reads back the three pushed WORDS (IP, CS=0x0008, FLAGS) via SS:BP and its own PUSHF shows IF CLEARED (mainline runs STI)

case (2): CPL0 #GP(0) (ljmp to the limit-0x100 segment 0x50 at offset 0x101 -- the A4-C02 fault class) through the 16-bit TRAP gate at vector 13: SP -> 0x6FF8 (exactly 8); four words read back (err=0, IP, CS, FLAGS); handler PUSHF shows IF PRESERVED; saved IP advanced 7, IRETW

case (3): CPL3->CPL0 through the 16-bit INT gate 0x42 onto TSS 0x10:0x6000: handler ESP == 0x6000-10 == 0x5FF6; five word slots (IP, CS=0x23, FLAGS, SP=0x5000, SS=0x2B); cross-priv IRETW restores ring 3 (ESP = the zero-extended SP word 0x00005000)

case (4): CPL3->CPL0 #NP(0x48) (ljmp to the NOT-PRESENT DPL3 code 0x48) through the 16-bit TRAP gate at vector 11: handler ESP == 0x6000-12 == 0x5FF4; six slots, the error word == 0x0048 (a NONZERO code proving the word errcode content)

case (5): CPL3->CPL0 through the 16-bit INT gate 0x44 onto the B=0 wrap stack (ring-3 code rewrites TSS.SS0:ESP0 = 0x30:0x00010004 and sets its ESP = 0x00025000): the five PUSHW stores wrap in the low 16 (SS@0002, SP@0000, FLAGS@FFFE, CS@FFFC, IP@FFFA); handler ESP == 0x0002FFFA -- the upper half 0x0002 is the OLD ring-3 ESP's upper (QEMU SET_ESP semantics: NOT esp0's 0x0001, NOT zeroed); the handler's BP-relative reads wrap through EA 0x0000/0x0002 and find the SP/SS words; the IRETW restores ESP = 0x00005000 (the frame saved only SP's low word -- the upper half is architecturally lost, both oracles)

case (7) CONTROLS: 32-bit INT gate 0x45 same-priv (ESP 0x7000 -> 0x6FF4, three dwords) and 32-bit INT gate 0x46 DPL3 cross-priv (ESP 0x6000 -> 0x5FEC, five dwords) -- byte-identical to the pre-fix shapes

witnesses.0x2004: case (1) handler SP == 0x6FFA (6-byte frame) -- ecx at exit
witnesses.0x2014: case (1) handler live FLAGS -- IF CLEARED by the interrupt gate (composite)
witnesses.0x2020: case (2) pushed IP word (the faulting ljmp)
witnesses.0x202c: case (2) handler live FLAGS -- IF PRESERVED by the trap gate (composite)
witnesses.0x2034: case (3) handler ESP == 0x00005FF6 (cross-priv 10-byte) -- esi at exit
witnesses.0x204c: case (4) handler ESP == 0x00005FF4 (cross-priv 12-byte) -- ebp at exit
witnesses.0x2068: case (5) handler ESP == 0x0002FFFA (the wrap witness: low wrapped, upper = the OLD ring-3 ESP's 0x0002) -- edi at exit
witnesses.0x2078: case (5) old SP word == 0x5000, read through the WRAPPED EA 0x0000 (composite)
witnesses.0x207c: case (5) old SS word == 0x002B, read through the WRAPPED EA 0x0002 (composite)
witnesses.exit_ebx: 0xB16B16B1 iff every composite check passes (case-2 SP/err, case-1 pushed CS, case-3 pushed SS, case-4 err 0x48, case-5 pushed SP/SS through the wrapped EAs, case-1 IF cleared, case-2 IF preserved, both 32-bit control ESPs)

oracle_notes.qemu_frame_construction: Verified against the pinned QEMU 8.2.2 source (target/i386/tcg/seg_helper.c do_interrupt_protected): shift = type>>3 selects PUSHW (16-bit gates) vs PUSHL; stores land at ssp + (sp & sp_mask) with sp_mask from the NEW stack's B bit cross-priv / the current SS same-priv; SET_ESP for a 16-bit stack keeps the OLD ESP register's upper half (NOT TSS.espN's high half -- case 5's ring-3 ESP upper 0x0002 != esp0's 0x0001 pins the rule exactly). QEMU implements the SDM exactly here: NO oracle gap for any case in this test.
oracle_notes.iretw_esp_restore: QEMU's helper_ret_protected (shift=0) pops the outer SP as a WORD and SET_ESP with the NEW SS's mask -- for a 32-bit outer SS (B=1) the popped word is ZERO-EXTENDED into ESP (golden: ESP=0x00005000 after every cross-priv IRETW here). pretfres/pretfoutpg pinned the same zero-extension for the 16-bit OUTER-SEGMENT case (H-02); this test pins it for the 16-bit OPERAND-SIZE (IRETW) case.
oracle_notes.null_selector_ljmp_deviation: OBSERVED BUT OUT OF SCOPE: the test originally triggered case (2) with a NULL-SELECTOR ljmp (SDM + QEMU helper_ljmp_protected: #GP(0)). The RTL's S_LJMP descriptor path does not precheck null (core_fetch_decode.svh's far_sel_bad dispatch covers only the far-CALL arm; core_seg_ljmp.svh:674 notes 'the far_sel_bad backstop is gone from this arm'), so it reads GDT[0] (zeros) and raises #NP(0) -- measured via +ven_faultlog: 'vec=11 err=00000000 pc=00000215' where QEMU delivers vec=13 err=0. An unrelated far-transfer selector-precheck defect; case (2) uses the offset-past-limit #GP(0) class (A4-C02, already gated by pjmpoff) instead. Reported to the RTL owner.

blocking_rtl_defect.status: RESOLVED 2026-08-04 -- the RTL inter-privilege IRETW recovery fix landed (core_iret.svh / core_gpr_wb.svh changed after first validation) and pint16f is now EQUIVALENT (419 records) and registered in RTL_SYS_TESTS. The text below is the historical record of the defect this test exposed at first validation.
blocking_rtl_defect.detail: The delivery (push) side of every case matches the golden exactly (all frame sizes, wrap stores, handler ESPs, IF semantics). The recovery side deviates: after a cross-priv 16-bit IRETW, the RTL installs ESP = (popped SS word << 16) | popped SP word (measured esp=0x002B5000 where the golden has 0x00005000). Root cause located (NOT fixed -- RTL frozen for this task): rtl/core/core_iret.svh S_IRET beat 4'd3 reads the outer ESP as a full DWORD ('iret_esp <= mem_rdata') with no int_gate_op16 word masking -- the dword at the 2-byte SP slot picks up the SS word as the upper half -- and rtl/core/core_gpr_wb.svh:725 commits iret_esp verbatim at S_IRET_SS. core_iret.svh's own beat-2 comment admits 'no gate exercises 16-bit inter-privilege IRET'. One-line-class fix: zero-extend the popped word for int_gate_op16 (matching the iret_eip handling at beat 4'd0). The divergence fires at n=324 (case-3 IRETW return) field=esp.
blocking_rtl_defect.negative_control_corollary: with the PRE-A4-H03 RTL the cross-priv deliveries would additionally push 32-BIT frames (handler ESPs 0x5FEC-style dword shapes vs the golden's word shapes) and never wrap case 5's stores -- the test discriminates both the push and the pop halves.

residuals.case6_paged_wrap: NOT IMPLEMENTED: the same-priv 16-bit delivery with SP near wrap and/or near a page boundary under paging (pxprobe/pxwalkd-style paging setup). The linear wrap mechanics are already pinned by case 5; the paged variant adds the walk interaction only. Left as a follow-up.
residuals.task_gate_16bit: 286 TSS task gates (IDT type 5 to a 16-bit TSS) are not exercised; out of the finding's frame-construction scope.

description: REVIEW_Aug4 A4-H03 regression for 16-bit protected-mode interrupt/trap gate frames. The pre-fix RTL built 32-BIT frames for cross-privilege 16-bit gates, charged 6 bytes even WITH an error code same-privilege, and never wrapped SP for a B=0 stack. This image drives seven cases in one run, all differentially graded against QEMU (an exact oracle here): (1) CPL0 software INT through a 16-bit interrupt gate -- 6-byte word frame, IF cleared; (2) CPL0 #GP(0) (offset-past-limit ljmp, the A4-C02 class) through the 16-bit trap gate at vector 13 -- 8-byte word frame, err=0, IF preserved; (3) CPL3->CPL0 software INT through a 16-bit interrupt gate -- 10-byte word frame on the TSS stack, five slots read back, cross-priv IRETW recovery; (4) CPL3->CPL0 #NP(0x48) through the 16-bit trap gate at vector 11 -- 12-byte word frame with a NONZERO error word; (5) CPL3->CPL0 onto a B=0 stack with TSS.esp0 = 0x00010004 -- the five PUSHW stores wrap in the low 16 and ESP's upper half is the OLD ESP's 0x0002 (0x0002FFFA); (7) 32-bit same/cross-priv interrupt-gate controls. ALL code segments are based at 0xF0000 so every offset is 16-bit clean (the word IP slots are exact and IRETW returns land). Handlers live in the 16-bit code segment 0x18 (D=0) and read their frames back via SS:BP-relative word slots; the discriminating witnesses fold into edi/esi/ebp/ecx/ebx before the isa-debug-exit so the step-7 RTL sys-diff compares them record-for-record. NO paging.

validation.golden_exit_record: edi=0x0002FFFA (case-5 wrap ESP) esi=0x00005FF6 (case-3) ebp=0x00005FF4 (case-4) ebx=0xB16B16B1 (composite) ecx=0x00006FFA (case-1)
validation.gate: bash verif/sys/run-sys-golden.sh pint16f (with pint16f temporarily appended to RTL_SYS_TESTS for the run; the registration edit was REVERTED afterward, per the task split -- the requester lands the registration)
validation.gate_result: steps 1-6 PASS (image builds, qemu exit 133, golden 419 records well-formed + transitions captured, comparator sys self-diff EQUIVALENT). Step 7 RED: RTL 1000 records (ran to the max-insn cap in a fault loop) vs golden 419; first divergence n=324 pc=0x000003ff field=esp expected 0x00005000 got 0x002B5000 (the 16-bit inter-privilege IRETW outer-ESP dword-read defect, blocking_rtl_defect). Flow (pc/cs) matches the golden through EVERY delivery -- the push side of A4-H03 is correct on this tree; only the cross-priv IRETW recovery deviates. Re-run once the RTL recovery fix lands.
